details.publicNotes:
A soul collector is an evil spirit trapped in a prison demiplane, anchored to reality only by a mystical soul decanter. The soul decanter constantly draws in nearby souls, both to strengthen the prison and to foil anyone the spirit might reach out to for aid. Yet, after centuries of imprisonment, some soul collectors have wrested control over their prison. Rather than strengthening the decanter, these souls now propagate their magic and turn prisoners' souls into a loyal undead army.

Those who encounter a soul collector in the mortal realm first come across their soul decanter, which the spirit can move around telekinetically to find more victims. It's only when they're sucked into the prison demiplane that they come across the soul collector face to face and experience the creature's true power. The soul collector often uses their spells, which they can cast using the decanter as a medium, to entice victims closer so that they can pull them in where the soul collector can face them directly and trap their soul.

Picturesque Prisons

A soul collector's prison demiplane often bears some relationship to their soul decanter. For instance, inside a clay decanter painted with the figures of mythical warriors, a soul collector broods among animate illusions of those same warriors. Inside a silver urn speckled with jewels, a soul collector bestrides a tiny planet under a silver, star-speckled sky. A prison demiplane is often a place of heartwrenching beauty to outsiders, although hideous in the eyes of the soul collector.

You transform the target into an undead creature with a level up to that allowed in the Creature Creation Rituals table. There are many versions of this ritual, each specific to a particular type of undead (one ritual for all zombies, one for skeletons, one for ghouls, and so on), and the rituals that create rare undead are also rare. Some forms of undead, such as liches, form using their own unique methods and can't be created with a version of create undead.

Critical Success The target becomes an undead creature of the appropriate type. If it's at least 4 levels lower than you, you can make it a minion. This gives it the minion trait, meaning it can use 2 actions when you command it, and commanding it is a single action that has the auditory and concentrate traits. You can have a maximum of four minions under your control. If it's intelligent and doesn't become a minion, the undead is helpful to you for awakening it, though it's still a horrid and evil creature. If it's unintelligent and doesn't become a minion, you can give it one simple command. It pursues that goal single-mindedly, ignoring any of your subsequent commands.

Success As critical success, except an intelligent undead that doesn't become your minion is only friendly to you, and an unintelligent undead that doesn't become your minion leaves you alone unless you attack it. It marauds the local area rather than following your command.

Failure You fail to create the undead.

Critical Failure You create the undead, but its soul, tortured by your foul necromancy, is full of nothing but hatred for you. It attempts to destroy you.

description.value: The soul collector is trapped on a finite demiplane. Typically, both time and gravity function normally within the demiplane, but its other features have been gradually molded into a foreboding environment that suits the soul collector's tastes. When a creature dies within the demiplane or has its soul pulled in by soulcall aura, its soul is trapped. The soul collector can release souls from the demiplane with imbue soul, but souls can otherwise only be freed by wish or the direct intervention of a deity. If a soul collector is destroyed, the demiplane collapses, freeing all trapped within.

The bridge between a soul collector's prison demiplane and the Universe is a magical soul decanter. The soul collector's senses extend out in a 120-foot radius around the decanter. They can cast spells, telepathically communicate, and use abilities with the occult trait with the decanter as the origin point. They can also use Fly to telekinetically move the decanter up to their fly Speed. A soul collector is immune to most effects from creatures outside of the demiplane. However, if the decanter is destroyed (Hardness 15, HP 150, BT 75), all living creatures within the demiplane are ejected and the demiplane is temporarily disconnected from the Universe. After 24 hours, a new soul decanter forms.

60 feet (centered on the soul decanter). All creatures with a soul in the aura are drawn into the prison demiplane, arriving as close to the soul collector as they were to the soul decanter. Unwilling creatures can attempt a @Check[will|dc:42] save to resist. Souls of creatures that die in the aura are drawn in automatically. Living creatures that remain in the demiplane for 1 hour are expelled back to their original space and are temporarily immune to the aura for 24 hours.
When a soul collector casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.OsOhx3TGIZ7AhD0P] or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.qwlh6aDgi86U3Q7H], the range increases to 120 feet.

When a soul collector uses create undead to make a non-mindless undead, they can use a soul from their prison. If they do, they can see through the undead's eyes and communicate with them telepathically at any distance. Additionally, they can graft excess soul energy onto the undead to make it seem alive. These undead receive an automatic result of 40 on Deception checks to pass as living creatures.
